svg.text: no-arg ctor wires TF-IDF + in-memory index for you ✓
index/remove return false on "already there / not there"
with the boolean style of its two siblings
THE CORE — thin orchestrator, not a god object
index: InvertedIndex (final) — the seam it depends on
synchronized indexDocument — reject if id already present
synchronized removeDocument — reject if id unknown
search(q, offset, limit) — the 3-line read path:
2. candidates = UNION of index.lookup(term) ← OR semantics
3. return rankingStrategy.rank(terms, candidates, index, offset, limit)
the engine never scores anything itself — ranking is 100% delegated ✓
search() is NOT synchronized while the writers ARE ⇒ a query can
straddle a concurrent re-index and see a doc for term A but not term B
OR-only: no AND, no phrase, no field filter, no fuzzy
rankingStrategy is a plain mutable field — swap is not volatile-safe
~60 lines. Everything expensive lives one layer down.
THE INDEX — three maps that must stay in lockstep
the seam a RankingStrategy is handed to score with
all 6 methods synchronized on the index
docTermFreq is the reverse map that makes
delete O(terms in doc), not O(all terms) ✓
empty postings lists are pruned on remove
every impl re-implements the same slice
score = Σ tf × idf, sort DESC
score = how many query terms hit
exists to CONTRAST with TF-IDF in the demo
THE MODEL — two immutable value objects, plus two exceptions
id: String (final) — validated non-blank in the ctor
fullText() = title + " " + content ← what gets tokenized
title and content are indexed as ONE bag of words
⇒ no field boost, no "title matters more" — a real gap
no tags, no metadata map, no updatedAt in this impl
carries the whole Document, not just an id ⇒ the caller
never round-trips back into the index to render a hit ✓
no snippet, no matchedTerms, no highlight offsets

g.text: WHY OR + TF-IDF WORKS
The candidate set is a plain UNION, so a
doc matching one rare term still shows up.
Precision is recovered by the SCORE, not
by the filter: a doc hitting both terms
sums two tf×idf contributions and floats up.
Cheap to build, ranks sanely.
AND semantics = intersect the posting sets
smallest-first. Phrase queries additionally
need positions in the postings — not stored.
THE LOCKING, HONESTLY
Two INDEPENDENT monitors: the engine's
and the index's. Writers hold both, so no
map is ever corrupted.
But search() holds NEITHER across its
many lookup() calls ⇒ it is atomic per
call, not per query.
Result: a doc reindexed mid-query can be
scored on stale tf. Fix = ReadWriteLock at
the engine, or an immutable index snapshot.
